title: Sable and the Autopsy
premise: Estate lawyer Gideon Halloran is summoned to read the will of Vivienne Sable, a woman declared dead seven years ago—yet the will is dated three days ago. Among her effects are twin letters: one confessing to a murder everyone believed solved, and one promising a second confession if Gideon can find who she really was before the estate's beneficiaries silence him. As Gideon traces Sable through forged identities, a drowned village, and a love affair with the case's original detective, he realizes the confession names his own late mentor as an accomplice. In the end, Gideon must choose between filing the truth and burning it, and discovers Sable staged her own second death to force one honest man into the open.
about_author: Paloma Pemberton is a former probate clerk from coastal Maine who spent a decade reading other people's final wishes before writing her own stories. She writes mysteries about paper trails, quiet towns, and the lies people notarize.

chapters.title: The Will That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Gideon Halloran, POV. Summoned to a rain-lashed manor, Gideon reads the will of Vivienne Sable—dead seven years by court record—and finds it dated last week. The beneficiaries watch him too closely. Emotional beat: professional unease curdling into fascination as he pockets two sealed letters no one else saw.

chapters.title: Twin Letters
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV, alone at night. The first letter confesses to the 2017 drowning of Thomas Reeve—the crime that closed this very town. The second promises 'the rest' if Gideon can find who Vivienne Sable was before she became a ghost. Beat: dread and thrill; his rule against unwinnable cases begins to crack.

chapters.title: Beneficiaries
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Sable's niece, Marguerite, who insists the will is fraudulent and hints Gideon should lose it. He notices the family's grief is rehearsed, their alibis identical. Beat: suspicion shifts from document to people; Gideon realizes someone expected him to refuse the reading entirely.

chapters.title: The Drowned Village
chapters.summary: Gideon travels to Ashcombe, the reservoir town submerged for a dam project where Sable grew up. An archivist recognizes her photo under another name. Beat: melancholy discovery—Sable lost everything in the flood, including a sister whose body was never recovered, and Thomas Reeve signed the dam order.

chapters.title: The Detective's Widow
chapters.summary: Gideon interviews Elena Marsh, widow of the detective who 'solved' Reeve's murder. She reveals her husband loved a woman named Vee—and that his suicide note named no killer at all. Beat: grief and tenderness complicate the mystery; love against duty surfaces as Elena begs Gideon to let the dead stay dead.

chapters.title: Forged in Probate
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV. Forensic examination shows the will's signature is genuine but its date impossible—unless Sable was alive until last month. Someone in the probate office helped her vanish, and that someone's initials match his mentor Aldous Wren. Beat: betrayal; loyalty vs. truth becomes personal.

chapters.title: What Aldous Knew
chapters.summary: Digging through Wren's old files, Gideon finds a retainer agreement linking Wren, Sable, and Reeve's company. Marguerite confronts him with a bribe and a threat. Beat: rising fear; Gideon understands the family didn't contest the will—they're trying to close the case before the second letter opens.

chapters.title: The Second Confession
chapters.summary: Following the second letter's clues to a boathouse, Gideon finds Sable alive, dying, and waiting. She confesses: Reeve drowned saving her sister during the flood, and the family buried the truth to keep the settlement money. Beat: catharsis and heartbreak; she chose Gideon because he never takes a case he can't close.

chapters.title: Silence or Signature
chapters.summary: Climax. Marguerite arrives to burn the evidence; Elena stands with Gideon. Sable dies holding the pen. Gideon must file the confession—which indicts his mentor's memory—or destroy it and protect everyone's peace. Beat: love against duty at knife's edge; he signs and files it, then hands Marguerite the choice to contest.

chapters.title: Closed
chapters.summary: Resolution, Gideon's POV. The truth reopens the Reeve case; the estate funds a memorial for the drowned village. Elena gives Gideon her husband's real suicide note—an apology, not a confession. Beat: bittersweet closure; Gideon closes his one unclosable case and finally stops being invisible himself.
